blocks.text: 29.2 Auto Filter
blocks.raw_html: 29.2 Auto Filter

blocks.text: Auto Filter is a filtering effect that modifies the incoming sound by applying frequency-selective filters. It offers various filter types and filter circuit types that emulate classic analog filters. The device’s LFO modulation and envelope follower help create dynamic, tone-sculpting effects. The envelope follower can respond to the filtered signal itself or to an external sidechain input.

blocks.text: 29.2.1 Filter Types
blocks.raw_html: 29.2.1 Filter Types

blocks.text: You can use the Filter Type chooser to select a filter from ten available types: Low-pass, High-pass, Band-pass, Notch, Morph, DJ, Comb, Resampling, Notch + LP, and Vowel.

blocks.text: The Low-pass filter attenuates frequencies above the cutoff. You can use it to reduce brightness or remove high-frequency content. You can switch the filter between 12 and 24 dB slopes.

blocks.text: High-pass allows frequencies above the cutoff frequency to pass while attenuating lower frequencies. It can be useful for removing low-frequency rumble or thinning out sounds. You can switch the filter between 12 and 24 dB slopes.

blocks.text: The Band-pass filter allows only a specific range of frequencies around the cutoff to pass, attenuating both lower and higher frequencies outside this range. This can be used to isolate a portion of the spectrum or create resonant, focused tones. You can switch the filter between 12 and 24 dB slopes.

blocks.text: Notch attenuates a narrow frequency range while leaving the surrounding frequencies largely unaffected. You can use it to remove specific frequencies or create subtle phasing-like effects. You can switch the filter between 12 and 24 dB slopes.

blocks.text: The Morph filter allows continuous morphing between low-pass and high-pass filtering, with band-pass behavior in between. It has four filter slopes you can choose from: 6, 12, 24, and 48 dB.

blocks.text: The DJ filter combines low-pass and high-pass filtering into a single bipolar control, similar to certain DJ mixer. Using values above zero filters out low frequencies and emphasizes high frequencies, while using values below zero filters out high frequencies and emphasizes low frequencies. Note that filter resonance is also affected: values near 0.0% result in a small boost of the emphasized frequencies, which grows progressively larger as values approach -100% or 100%.

blocks.text: 29.2.3 LFO Controls
blocks.raw_html: 29.2.3 LFO Controls

blocks.text: Auto Filter can apply independent LFO modulation to the left and right channels, allowing the modulation to be offset across the stereo field. Use the LFO Stereo Mode toggle at the bottom of the display to switch between two stereo offset modes: Phase and Spin.
blocks.raw_html: Auto Filter can apply independent LFO modulation to the left and right channels, allowing the modulation to be offset across the stereo field. Use the LFO Stereo Mode toggle at the bottom of the display to switch between two stereo offset modes: Phase and Spin.

blocks.text: Phase keeps both LFOs at the same frequency, but can set the two LFO waveforms out of phase with each other, creating stereo movement. The left and right modulation channels can be offset in degrees using the LFO Phase control. At 180°, the channels are perfectly out of phase, so that when one LFO reaches its peak, the other is at its minimum. The Spin mode detunes the two LFO rates relative to each other by a percentage set via the LFO Spin control. When Phase is set to 0° or Spin is set to 0%, the left and right channels are modulated identically.

blocks.text: 29.2.4 Envelope Follower Controls
blocks.raw_html: 29.2.4 Envelope Follower Controls

blocks.text: The envelope controls allow you to specify how the envelope modulation affects the filter frequency.

blocks.text: The Envelope Attack slider at the bottom of the display sets how the envelope responds to rising input signals. Low values result in a fast response to input levels, whereas high values integrate any changes gradually, creating a looser, slower response. Think of it as adding inertia to the response.

blocks.text: 29.7 Channel EQ
blocks.raw_html: 29.7 Channel EQ

blocks.text: Inspired by EQs found on classic mixing desks, Channel EQ is a simple, yet flexible three-band EQ, fine-tuned to provide musical results for a variety of audio material.

blocks.text: 29.15 EQ Eight
blocks.raw_html: 29.15 EQ Eight

blocks.text: The EQ Eight effect is an equalizer featuring up to eight parametric filters per input channel, useful for changing a sound’s timbre.

blocks.text: The input signal can be processed using one of three modes: Stereo, L/R and M/S. Stereo mode uses a single curve to filter both channels of a stereo input equally. L/R mode provides an independently adjustable filter curve for the left and right channels of a stereo input; M/S mode (Mid/Side) provides the same functionality for signals that have been recorded using M/S encoding. In all modes, the frequency spectrum of the output is displayed behind the filter curves when the Analyze switch is on.

In all modes, the frequency spectrum of the output is displayed behind the filter curves when the Analyze switch is on.

blocks.text: When using the L/R and M/S modes, both curves are displayed simultaneously for reference, although only the active channel is editable. The Edit switch indicates the active channel, and is used to toggle between the two curves.

owner_requirements.title: frequency-selective processing
owner_requirements.text: Incoming device-chain audio is filtered by the selected filter. LFO and envelope follower can modulate the filtering; the envelope follower can use internal or external sidechain audio. Exact internal detector tap is not established: the opening summary says filtered signal, whereas the sidechain section says input source.

owner_requirements.title: filter selection
owner_requirements.text: The documented Filter Type chooser offers Low-pass, High-pass, Band-pass, Notch, Morph, DJ, Comb, Resampling, Notch + LP and Vowel. Numeric enum mapping and mode-change state retention are U.

owner_requirements.title: low/high/band/notch slope choices
owner_requirements.text: Low-pass attenuates above cutoff; High-pass attenuates below; Band-pass passes a range around cutoff; Notch attenuates a narrow range. Each offers 12 and 24 dB slope choices. These labels do not establish measured slope at cutoff, Q law, pole locations or coefficients.

owner_requirements.title: Morph filter slopes
owner_requirements.text: Morph traverses low-pass through band-pass to high-pass with increasing Morph. Its documented slope options are 6, 12, 24 and 48 dB. Transition law and endpoint transfer functions are U.

owner_requirements.title: DJ bipolar control
owner_requirements.text: DJ uses a bipolar Control: above zero removes low frequencies; below zero removes high frequencies. Emphasis grows as values approach −100%/+100%. The description does not establish a transparent 0% transfer function or a numeric resonance law.

owner_requirements.title: Comb, Resampling, Vowel and Notch + LP
owner_requirements.text: Comb produces repeated peaks/notches. Resampling continuously resamples at a rate determined by cutoff, reducing high-frequency content with aliasing. Vowel emphasizes vocal formants. Notch + LP combines a notch with low-pass rolloff, with 12/24 dB choices. Delay lengths, sampling ratios, formant tables and coefficients are U.

owner_requirements.title: frequency and vowel controls
owner_requirements.text: Freq sets cutoff except DJ, where Control replaces Freq, and Vowel, where Pitch shifts formants in semitones. For Vowel, Formant replaces Res and traverses a, e, i, o, u. No numeric pitch/formant domain or map is established.

owner_requirements.title: resonance availability
owner_requirements.text: Res emphasizes cutoff for applicable filters. Res has no effect in Resampling and is grayed out. Exact resonance scale, instability boundary and self-oscillation are U.

owner_requirements.title: filter Morph variants
owner_requirements.text: Morph, Comb, Notch + LP and Vowel have Morph controls. Comb moves from peaks at low Morph toward notches at high Morph at cutoff multiples. In Notch + LP the notch approaches cutoff as Morph rises and reaches cutoff at 100%. Vowel Morph increasingly normalizes formant gain. Exact frequency/gain interpolation is U.

owner_requirements.title: filter display and dragging
owner_requirements.text: The display shows selected filter curve, modulated left/right curves and output spectrum. Dragging its handle changes Freq and Res, or Pitch and Formant for Vowel. Pixel mapping, display FFT and other modes’ handle mapping are U.

owner_requirements.title: modulation-section selection
owner_requirements.text: LFO and Envelope sections below the display expose their section parameters at the display bottom when selected. Selection alone supplies no documented reset or sound-change rule.

owner_requirements.title: stereo LFO modes
owner_requirements.text: Phase keeps L/R LFO frequency equal with offset in degrees: 180° places one peak at the other minimum. Spin detunes L/R rates by its percentage. Phase 0° or Spin 0% modulates channels identically. Random-waveform caveats belong to REQ-DEVICE-AF-016.

owner_requirements.title: phase-offset time-mode dependency
owner_requirements.text: LFO Phase Offset shifts both waveform starting points only for tempo-synced beat divisions or sixteenth-note time modes. Its parameter has no effect in the other documented time modes. Transport-start reset, phase origin and seek behavior are U.

owner_requirements.title: LFO quantization
owner_requirements.text: Steps divides an LFO cycle into the number of intervals selected by LFO Steps. S&H quantizes LFOs to the LFO S&H beat-time setting. Exact sampling edge, interpolation and legal divisions are U.

owner_requirements.title: LFO amount and time modes
owner_requirements.text: LFO Amt controls modulation depth and can combine with envelope modulation. Rate is expressed in Hz, seconds, synced beat divisions or sixteenth-note values according to Mode; Time mode labels the control Time. Rate domains, tempo-change smoothing and amount scaling are U.

owner_requirements.title: LFO waveform controls
owner_requirements.text: Wave offers Sine, Triangle, Saw, Square, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Wander and S&H. S&H generates random positive and negative modulation. Wander and S&H disable Spin with a gray control. LFO Morph transforms waveform shape; for S&H it is replaced by Smooth. Random distributions, seeds, repeatability and waveform equations are U.

owner_requirements.title: envelope attack and release
owner_requirements.text: Envelope modulates filter frequency. Lower Attack responds faster to rising input; higher Attack integrates changes more slowly. Lower Release responds faster to falling level; higher Release extends decay. No detector transfer, time-constant definition or sum/clamp law with LFO is established.

owner_requirements.title: envelope Hold
owner_requirements.text: With Envelope Hold on the entire attack phase completes before release starts. Exact attack-completion criterion, retrigger and release interruption are U.

owner_requirements.title: envelope sample-and-hold
owner_requirements.text: Envelope S&H enables envelope quantization at the beat-time value selected with Envelope S&H Rate. Exact clock edge and off-state phase retention are U.

owner_requirements.title: envelope polarity/depth
owner_requirements.text: Envelope control determines direction and extent of modulation. Numeric endpoints and polarity-to-cutoff map for each filter are U.

owner_requirements.title: input Drive
owner_requirements.text: Drive applies drive before filtering. At 0.0% the drive contribution is described as unaltered; increasing Drive produces progressively greater distortion/saturation. This does not prove whole-device identity, a transfer curve, headroom or oversampling.

owner_requirements.title: circuit selection and availability
owner_requirements.text: Filter Circuit offers SVF, DFM, MS2 and PRD and affects only Low-pass, High-pass, Band-pass, Notch and Morph. SVF is described as clean with distortion possible above zero Drive; DFM has distortion feedback; MS2 soft-clips resonance; PRD has no explicit resonance limiting. Architectural descriptions are documentary characterizations, not recovered algorithms.

owner_requirements.title: output, Clip and Dry/Wet
owner_requirements.text: Clip soft-clips effect output and its LED flashes on clipping. Output sets processed-signal level; Dry/Wet balances processed and unprocessed audio. Exact threshold, clipping function, gain range, mix law and stage ordering beyond named input Drive/output clipping remain U.

owner_requirements.title: external sidechain routing
owner_requirements.text: The Sidechain Section toggle exposes controls; External enables external triggering. External Source selects a signal, and External Tapping Point offers Pre FX, Post FX or Post Mixer. Missing/deleted source, routing cycles, compensation and device off-state are U.

owner_requirements.title: sidechain mix and gain
owner_requirements.text: Mix 100% follows external sidechain exclusively; Mix 0% follows internal sidechain only. SC Gain changes external detector input level, not source-track volume. Mix interpolation, internal tap and detector calibration are U.

owner_requirements.title: sidechain Listen
owner_requirements.text: Sidechain Listen bypasses Auto Filter output and exposes sidechain input for monitoring. Exact monitored stage, stereo/mono relationship, gain and switching ramp are U.

owner_requirements.title: sidechain filtering
owner_requirements.text: SC Filter enables frequency-selective detection. Sidechain Filter Frequency sets cutoff; low-shelf, peak and high-shelf use signed gain for boost/cut, with shelf response leveling at gain rather than continued rolloff. Sidechain Filter Q controls bandwidth. The complete Type enum is U: B59 lists band-pass while B63 instead explains Notch. Neither a merged enum nor a correction is inferred.

owner_requirements.title: mono sidechain
owner_requirements.text: By default the sidechain is converted to mono, giving identical L/R envelope modulation. The Mono Sidechain context-menu option disables that conversion. Off-state stereo detector mapping, summing coefficients and interactions with Listen/LFO are U.

owner_requirements.title: retained current-device state
owner_requirements.text: The retained named Auto Filter default has an AutoFilter2 root and the schema declares its filter, LFO, envelope, sidechain and output vocabulary. Exact file observations are retained in package-values.json. Filename default does not prove a runtime constructor default; HiQuality naming does not prove oversampling.

owner_requirements.title: unresolved lifecycle and exact audio
owner_requirements.text: Every D12 clause remains exact-12.4.3 U. Automation scheduling, transport restart/seek, undo/redo, edit cancellation, invalid fields/ranges, saved-state migration, routing source failure, sample-rate/block-size changes, deletion and teardown have no outcome oracle. Numerical response, modulation kernels, stochastic laws, smoothing, latency, clipping thresholds and tolerances are U. Legacy AutoFilter behavior is a separate unmapped obligation; the current manual is not its behavioral source.

owner_requirements.title: three-band signal processing
owner_requirements.text: Channel EQ is a three-band audio equalizer. Its host chain position determines incoming signal; insertion/routing/preset lifecycle belongs to the rack/host owner. No processing order or channel-coupling matrix is established.

owner_requirements.title: HP 80 Hz switch
owner_requirements.text: HP 80 Hz toggles a high-pass filter. Its label supplies the documented nominal frequency, not a measured −3 dB location, order, slope or coefficient set.

owner_requirements.title: adaptive low shelf
owner_requirements.text: Low controls a low shelf tuned to 100 Hz over −15 to +15 dB; its curve changes dynamically relative to applied gain. Q-versus-gain law, gain normalization and meaning of tuning are U.

owner_requirements.title: sweepable mid peak
owner_requirements.text: Mid gain ranges from −12 to +12 dB. Its frequency slider sets peak center over 120 Hz–7.5 kHz. Bandwidth and exact response around center are U.

owner_requirements.title: asymmetric High control
owner_requirements.text: Positive High boosts a high shelf up to +15 dB. Negative High combines shelf attenuation with low-pass: from 0 toward −15 dB, low-pass cutoff moves from 20 kHz to 8 kHz. Intermediate mapping, shelf frequency and filter slope are U.

owner_requirements.title: spectrum and curves
owner_requirements.text: Visualization shows resulting filter curves and processed-signal spectrum in real time. FFT, window, amplitude calibration, pixel rendering and update latency are U.

owner_requirements.title: processed output gain
owner_requirements.text: Output adjusts gain of processed signal. Track mixer laws do not establish this control’s conversion, domain, saturation or smoothing. Placing Saturator after it is a documented use case, not a Channel EQ distortion algorithm.

owner_requirements.title: retained state vocabulary
owner_requirements.text: Schema ChannelEq declares HighpassOn, LowShelfGain, MidGain, MidFrequency, HighShelfGain and Gain; Boom Capture.adv retains concrete values. Raw saved values do not establish displayed dB conversion, constructor defaults or accepted ranges.

owner_requirements.title: lifecycle and response gaps
owner_requirements.text: Exact-build D12 applicability, complete stereo response, automation, undo/redo, persistence, invalid text/state, cancel, bypass, sample-rate/block-size changes and teardown remain U. Cases below retain finite probes without success oracles.

owner_requirements.title: filter count and channel modes
owner_requirements.text: Up to eight parametric filters per input channel are documented. Stereo applies one curve equally to both input channels; L/R independently edits L and R; M/S provides independently editable curves for the documented M/S-encoded signal use. Encoding/decoding matrix and normalization are U.

owner_requirements.title: active editing channel
owner_requirements.text: In L/R and M/S both curves are visible, but only the Edit-selected channel is editable. Edit toggles curves. Mode-switch copying, inactive-value retention and saved selection are U.

owner_requirements.title: eight response choices
owner_requirements.text: Per band the chooser offers 48 and 12 dB/octave low cut, low shelf, peak, notch, high shelf, and 12 and 48 dB/octave high cut, in that documented vertical order. Response labels establish directional selection, not coefficient sets, exact cutoff attenuation or numeric stored enums.

owner_requirements.title: independent band enable
owner_requirements.text: Each band has its own activator under the chooser. More than one filter can share parameters for stronger combined filtering. Bypass ramps, internal execution/CPU measurements and summation order are U.

owner_requirements.title: graph editing and selection
owner_requirements.text: Dragging dots horizontally changes frequency and vertically changes gain for gain-supporting filters. Drag-enclosing multiple dots selects them for simultaneous mouse or arrow-key changes. Selection geometry, key increment and mixed-response constraints are U.

owner_requirements.title: Q and cut/notch restrictions
owner_requirements.text: Alt on Windows or Option on macOS while dragging adjusts Q. Low cut, Notch and High cut do not support gain changes; vertical dragging changes Q for these response types. Numeric Q range and bandwidth convention are U.

owner_requirements.title: expanded display
owner_requirements.text: The title-bar button moves the display between device chain and main window. In expanded view all eight filters can be edited simultaneously in Device View. Layout sizes, focus transfer and hidden-state persistence are U.

owner_requirements.title: output spectrum visibility
owner_requirements.text: Analyze displays output spectrum behind curves in every processing mode. The output spectrum is shown by default according to the manual; Analyze off disables spectrum view. FFT/window, channel combination, display latency and runtime constructor default are U.

owner_requirements.title: Adaptive Q
owner_requirements.text: With Adaptive Q enabled, Q increases as boost/cut amount increases. Exact gain-to-Q relation, shelf applicability and interaction with Scale are U; AdaptiveQFactor=1.12 in one file is not such a law.

owner_requirements.title: held Audition
owner_requirements.text: Enabling Audition with the headphone icon permits temporary single-filter solo by clicking and holding a filter dot, so only that filter’s effect is heard. Release ends the described temporary hold; exact audition transfer, transitions and transport interaction are U.

owner_requirements.title: numeric editing
owner_requirements.text: Clicking near a band number selects it for Freq/Gain/Q dials or direct numeric-field entry. Text parsing, units, malformed input and out-of-range normalization are U.

owner_requirements.title: global Gain
owner_requirements.text: Global Gain adjusts output level. Its range, dB conversion, processing order relative to oversampling and smoothing are U.

owner_requirements.title: Scale eligibility
owner_requirements.text: Scale adjusts gain of all gain-supporting filters, excluding low cut, notch and high cut. Scale domain, arithmetic law, sign/inversion and parameter mutation versus effective-gain behavior are U.

owner_requirements.title: Oversampling context option
owner_requirements.text: Oversampling is available from the device title-bar context menu. When enabled, internal processing is documented at twice the current sample rate. This is a D12 rate statement only; resampling filters, latency, precision, transition handling and exact target operation are U.

owner_requirements.title: response-specific sound

quotes.quote: Auto Filter is a filtering effect that modifies the incoming sound by applying frequency-selective filters. It offers various filter types and filter circuit types that emulate classic analog filters. The device’s LFO modulation and envelope follower help create dynamic, tone-sculpting effects. The envelope follower can respond to the filtered signal itself or to an external sidechain input.

By default, Auto Filter uses its input source to trigger the envelope follower. However, you can set the device to respond to an external sidechain signal instead. To access the external sidechain parameters, click on the Sidechain Section toggle in the upper left corner of the device.

quotes.quote: The Sidechain Filter Frequency control sets the cutoff frequency for the sidechain filter. Use the Type chooser to select a filter from the following: low-shelf, peak, high-shelf, low-pass, band-pass, and high-pass.

The low-pass filter attenuates frequencies above the cutoff. High-pass allows frequencies above the cutoff frequency to pass while attenuating lower frequencies. Notch attenuates a narrow frequency range while leaving the surrounding frequencies largely unaffected. You can use the Sidechain Filter Q slider to set the filter’s bandwidth.
